flawed_step: The attempted implication from Hamiltonian cycles in every vertex-deleted graph to a Hamiltonian cycle in G is unjustified: those cycles need not be compatible. The Petersen graph satisfies the premise but not the conclusion.
counterexample: Let indices be modulo 5. Take vertices a_0,...,a_4,b_0,...,b_4 and edges a_i a_{i+1}, a_i b_i, and b_i b_{i+2} for every i. This is the connected Petersen graph. For every k, deleting a_k leaves the Hamiltonian cycle (a_{k+1},a_{k+2},a_{k+3},a_{k+4},b_{k+4},b_{k+2},b_k,b_{k+3},b_{k+1},a_{k+1}). Deleting b_k leaves the Hamiltonian cycle (a_k,a_{k+1},b_{k+1},b_{k+3},a_{k+3},a_{k+2},b_{k+2},b_{k+4},a_{k+4},a_k). Each displayed consecutive pair is one of the specified edges, and each cycle contains all nine remaining vertices exactly once. To check that G itself is not Hamiltonian, partition its vertices into A={a_i} and B={b_i}. A Hamiltonian cycle would use a positive even number of the five spokes a_i b_i, hence either two or four. With two spokes, its restriction to each of the two 5-cycles A and B would be a spanning path. The two spoke indices would therefore have to differ by 1 modulo 5 in A and by 2 modulo 5 in B, which is impossible. With four spokes, let k be the index of the unused spoke. Degree constraints force the selected non-spoke edges to be a_{k-1}a_k, a_ka_{k+1}, a_{k+2}a_{k-2} and b_{k-2}b_k, b_kb_{k+2}, b_{k-1}b_{k+1}. Together with the four spokes, these form two disjoint 5-cycles, not one Hamiltonian 10-cycle. Thus G has no Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary: A step-by-step proof attempt fails at the claimed implication. The explicitly defined Petersen graph is connected, every one-vertex deletion has the displayed Hamiltonian cycle, and a complete spoke-count argument proves that the graph itself is non-Hamiltonian.
